profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged Verizon Wireless Mew Building, sits in Southlake, Tarrant County, Texas near Kirkwood Boulevard. The name itself signals wireless-network infrastructure rather than commercial colocation space, consistent with a mobile switching center or radio-network equipment site supporting Verizon cellular service in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. The word Mew in the name could not be explained by any source consulted this session. No nearby street, subdivision, or landmark by that name was found, so it may be an internal Verizon building code, a data-entry artifact from whatever source the original mapper used, or something else not documented anywhere accessible. More notable is how the telecom=data_center tag was added to this record: the edit history shows it was added inside a much larger changeset of 362 individual changes whose own changeset comment reads only added houses, indicating the edit was very likely part of a bulk residential-housing mapping pass and that the data-center tag on this particular way was added incidentally or by mistake rather than as a deliberate, sourced classification. This is the weakest tag provenance found anywhere in this Verizon record cluster alongside the Sandy City, Utah MapRoulette tag. Texas is outside the nine-state footprint where Verizon operates as the legacy incumbent local exchange carrier, so no regional Bell heritage explanation applies here. Given both the unexplained building name and the accidental-looking tagging history, this record should be treated as unconfirmed and possibly mistagged rather than a verified data center, and no capacity, square footage, tier rating, or year-built figures are asserted.
